floor_history.headline: First honest pure-C measurement of motion_Close (floor 21->20, structure an exact match) — and a corpus-wide kill: gcc-2.7.2 o32 reserves REG_PARM_STACK_SPACE=16 for every C-level call, so the target'

Floor 20->17 from statement order alone; then H3 KILLED with the instrumented cc1 — global.c's allocno priority forces count->$s0 / p->$s1 for every C form that emits the target's instruction sequence

Session 2's H3 kill is FALSIFIED: global.c breaks an exact allocno priority TIE by declaration order, the target's $s0=p/$s1=count roles ARE C-reachable, floor 17->16, and hand-asm signal S-c is retra

Permuter found a POLICY-CLEAN route to floor 16: a single-level FAKE-annotated do{p=&D_8008D070;}while(0) wrap wins $s0 for p by a strict allocno priority margin (loop-depth ref weighting, 34285 vs 30
Floor 20->13 recovered and independently re-measured (the discarded s5 run's form, banked into candidate.c at last), and frontier F5 KILLED structurally: local-alloc/global.c scan hard regs ascending

frontier.hypothesis: F7 (the only remaining nominally-open bucket, worth 2) - the beqz delay slot (target holds a nop where ours holds `sw s0,16`) and the prologue save ORDER (target saves s0,s1,ra at 4/8/12 ascending; ours emits ra,s1 then s0 into the delay slot).
frontier.mechanism: Both come out of mips.c's save_restore_insns emission plus reorg.c's delay-slot fill of the guard branch. Our build has a free delay slot to fill precisely because it has three saves to place and a 32-byte frame to build; the target's frame is 16 with a different save order and leaves the slot empty. The two halves are probably one phenomenon, and both are downstream of the frame that H1 already proves unreachable - so this may well close out as a third structural kill rather than 2 recoverable points. That is worth establishing explicitly, because it decides whether motion_Close has ANY reachable gradient left.
frontier.next_probe: Compile the floor-13 chassis with -da and read f13.c.dbr (reorg) plus the prologue emission: does the `sw s0` land in the slot because reorg found it the only eligible insn, or because save_restore_insns ordered the saves that way? Then test whether ANY pure-C body with a call and two callee-saved locals under this toolchain emits an empty guard-branch delay slot - a corpus scan of the oracle build for `beq $X,$zero` immediately followed by `nop` inside a function prologue answers it in one pass. If none exists, the last 2 points are dead too and motion_Close is fully explained at floor 13.

frontier.hypothesis: F8 - motion_Close is an escalation candidate, and the next session should be prepared for the driver to route it there rather than spend more sessions on a floor with 11/13 points structurally proven unreachable.
frontier.mechanism: Two independent frozen-toolchain mechanisms (H1 REG_PARM_STACK_SPACE = 16 for the frame; ascending first-free hard-reg scan with no MIPS REG_ALLOC_ORDER for $v0-vs-$t0) each prove a distinct bucket unreachable from any C source, not merely un-found. Together they account for 11 of the 13 remaining points. This is exactly the shape that distinguishes 'the search has not found it' from 'no C input to this compiler produces these bytes'.
frontier.next_probe: Do NOT self-dispose - exhaustion is the driver's call and the ladder still has untried modalities (forensics / rederive / synthesis). What a future session CAN do cheaply is strengthen or refute the record: run `python3 tools/scan_hand_coded.py --single motion_Close` and record the signal tier verbatim (session 3 retracted the earlier S-c signal, so the current tier is unknown), and finish F7 above. Those two results are what an escalation entry would have to cite, and they are useful regardless of routing.

frontier.hypothesis: F4b (carried forward, now much lower value) - lengthen count's live range so p-first order and p's priority win can hold with a SMALLER device than the three-level wrap.
frontier.mechanism: The floor-13 form already achieves p-first order AND p in $s0; F4b's original purpose (recovering the 2 positional points) is therefore ALREADY BANKED. What remains of it is purely a policy simplification: a three-level nested do-while(0) is a heavier device than a single level and a reviewer may push back on it, so a form reaching 13 with a single-level wrap (or none) would be strictly better to submit even at identical score.
frontier.next_probe: Sweep bodies that lengthen count's live range without adding a count reference - an intervening real computation the target also performs, so count spans it - and check whether p at 8 weighted refs / live_length 8 can beat a count whose live_length grew back to 8 while p is assigned first. Measure score AND the allocno table per form (BB2_ALLOC_DEBUG=1). Success criterion is score 13 with wrap depth < 3, not a lower score.
